title: Techcombank Hanoi International Marathon Review: Hanoi's Homegrown Race Hits Edition Five
meta_description: What to expect from the 5th edition of the Techcombank Hanoi International Marathon on 4 Oct 2026: six distances, Hanoi's autumn running conditions, and what's still unannounced.
dek: Six distances, an early-October date that catches Hanoi at its autumn best, and a race now entering its fifth year — here's our take on Vietnam's capital-city marathon.
verdict: The Techcombank Hanoi International Marathon is carving out a useful niche: a genuine full marathon in Hanoi at the best time of year to run there, with enough shorter-distance options to pull in a broad field. The fifth edition signals staying power, and the October date — Hanoi's dry, cool autumn window — is arguably the strongest selling point. The gaps are real: no confirmed start venue, no registration details yet, and less of a known-quantity course than the city's other major races. It's one to watch rather than one to book flights for just yet, but runners already based in northern Vietnam should keep it on their radar as the details land.

sections.heading: Why October in Hanoi Matters
paragraphs: Anyone who has run in Hanoi between May and September knows the deal: 33°C, punishing humidity, and a sun that feels personal. The Techcombank Hanoi International Marathon's 4 October 2026 date sidesteps all of that, landing in the city's brief, glorious autumn window when daytime highs settle into the mid-to-high 20s and the overnight humidity finally breaks [1].

It's the same seasonal logic that makes the city's November races popular, and October arguably edges it: you get the cool air before the year-end haze settles in [1]. For a full marathon in a tropical capital, the calendar placement here does a lot of the heavy lifting — this is about as comfortable as 42.195 km gets in Hanoi [1].

sections.heading: Six Distances, One Start Line (Wherever That Is)
paragraphs: The race offers six distance categories: a full marathon (42.195 km), half marathon (21.1 km), 10 km, 5 km, 3 km, and a 1.5 km fun run [1]. That range is unusually wide — most Vietnamese road races top out at three or four distances — and it signals an event that wants to be a city-wide festival rather than a hardcore runner's-only affair [1].

The catch is that the exact start venue within Hanoi hasn't been named yet [1]. Past editions have used routes around Hoan Kiem Lake and the Red River dike roads, but without a confirmed 2026 course map, runners can't yet plan pacing or logistics beyond 'somewhere in Hanoi' [1]. For a fifth-edition race, the continued venue ambiguity is the single biggest thing holding it back from feeling like a finished product [1].

sections.heading: Registration and the Information Gap
paragraphs: As of early August 2026, registration has not yet opened and no pricing has been published [1]. The official site at marathonhn.com is live but sparse, offering confirmation of the date and distances without the kind of detail — start time, cut-off limits, aid station map, bag-drop policy — that runners look for when committing to a race [1].

This isn't unusual for Vietnamese races of this scale: registration windows often open closer to race day than international runners are used to, and early detail tends to come through local running-community channels before it hits the official site [1]. Runners already plugged into the Hanoi running scene will likely hear about registration through word of mouth or Facebook groups well before the website updates [1].

sections.heading: The Field: Who This Race Is For
paragraphs: With distances spanning from a 1.5 km fun run to a full marathon, the event is designed to pull in everyone from serious marathoners to families looking for a Sunday activity [1]. The full marathon distance gives it credibility as a competitive event, while the shorter options make it accessible to the large recreational running community that has grown rapidly in Hanoi over the past five years [1].

That broad appeal is the race's strategic strength, but it also means the marathon field is likely to be modest compared to the shorter distances — a common pattern in multi-distance Asian road races where the full marathon is the prestige distance but the 10 km and half marathon draw the bulk of the entries [1].

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If you're based in northern Vietnam or planning to be in Hanoi in early October, this is worth a serious look — the date is excellent, the distance range covers whatever you're training for, and the fifth-edition milestone suggests the event has figured out the basics [1]. For international runners planning a dedicated race trip, the incomplete venue and registration picture makes it hard to recommend booking flights right now, but it's absolutely one to track as more details surface [1].

The Techcombank branding and the growing reputation of Hanoi's running scene give this race a credible foundation; what it needs next is a locked-in start line and a registration page. When those land, it'll be much easier to call [1].
